messages:
javier: Hey folks — trying to install redwoodctl on Pop!_OS (Ubuntu 22.04). Installer script ran but when I type `redwoodctl` I get `bash: /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl: Permission denied` :confused:

mia: Can you paste the install command and `ls -l /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl` output?

javier: Ran `curl -fsSL https://get.redwood.ai | sh` (default). Installer said `Installed to /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl`.

javier: ls -l output:
```
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 123456 Mar 12 12:10 /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl
```

javier: looks like it isn't executable. odd that the script didn't chmod +x.

andre: That usually means the installer missed the chmod step or the filesystem blocked execs. Try `sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl` then `which redwoodctl` and `redwoodctl version`.

javier: did that — now `redwoodctl` runs but `redwoodctl login` says `no default profile found` even though I created a profile earlier at `~/.config/redwood/profiles.json`.

mia: Which version did you install? `redwoodctl version` output? Also paste `cat ~/.config/redwood/profiles.json` (no secrets) or at least the keys.

javier: version v0.9.4. profiles.json keys look like: `{"profiles": {"personal": {"endpoint": "https://api.redwood.ai"}}}`

helen: CLI v0.9 -> v0.10 changed config path to `~/.redwood/config.json` (we added migration). v0.9 used `~/.config/redwood/`. The installer should have run a migration step but if installer skipped it you'll see "no default profile".

sam: Run `redwoodctl doctor` — it checks config schema and suggests migration commands. If doctor not present in v0.9, you can run the migration helper from the new binary: `redwoodctl migrate-config --from ~/.config/redwood/profiles.json`

javier: I ran `redwoodctl doctor` and it printed: `config schema version: 1 (legacy). run 'redwoodctl migrate-config' to upgrade`. Ran migration and now `redwoodctl profiles list` shows `personal`.

javier: Next issue: `redwoodctl login --profile personal` opens my browser but our company SSO blocks popups on this machine (no browser access). Is there a headless/device code flow?

andre: Yes, `redwoodctl login --no-browser` will print a device code and URL. Use that on any device to complete auth. There's also `--device` alias.

javier: `redwoodctl login --no-browser` worked. However when I run `redwoodctl local-serve --profile personal` the local server still says `unauthenticated` and warns `no token found at ~/.redwood/token.json`. I do have a token in `~/.config/redwood/token.json` (legacy path).

helen: Ah — another legacy path problem. The migrate step should have moved `token.json` too but if your installer failed earlier (chmod missing) the migration might have aborted. Quick workaround: `mkdir -p ~/.redwood && mv ~/.config/redwood/token.json ~/.redwood/token.json` then restart local-serve. We'll push a CLI fix to auto-detect both paths.

devbot: deploy pipeline: patch branch `devex/cli-config-detect` created to check legacy paths for tokens and profiles. CI triggered. :rocket:

sam: Also note on some distros `/usr/local` can be mounted with `noexec`. If you ever see exec errors after chmod, try installing to `$HOME/.local/bin` or use the recommended installer flag `sh -s -- --install-dir $HOME/.local/bin` (our installer supports `--install-dir`).

javier: Followed to move token, restarted. `redwoodctl local-serve` now picks up token and local dev server starts. Everything green. Thanks all. :party_parrot:

mia: Filing a small doc update and an installer test to ensure chmod +x and migration steps run even when `/usr/local` is weird. Assigning to @andre to add the test.

andre: Got it — I'll add an integration test and include a `--no-chmod` and `--install-dir` CI matrix. Also adding more helpful error messages when migration fails.

javier: Confirmed fixed on my machine. Closing thread. :thumbsup:
